doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Introductions and what Snooky and Gerald are doing now
summary: Monk Rowe welcomes the two men; Snooky is freelancing, Gerald teaches at UCLA and leads his band.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We’re filming today for the Hamilton Jazz Archive and we’re in California and we’re also in musician’s heaven, because today we have two giants of jazz music — Mr. Gerald Wilson and Mr. Snooky Young, who between them have accounted for some of the greatest recordings of trumpet music and also some of the greatest compositions and arrangements, and it’s a real pleasure to have you gentlemen here. Welcome.
Before the cameras were rolling we got a taste of some history between these two gentlemen, and I want to ask you what you’re doing right now though. You said you’re busy, I know you’re busy.
Actually, I’m just freelancing. I’ve been out of work now for three years, but I’m not unhappy about that.
You’re filling in the time I bet.
You’re with the Tonight Show Band here tonight, and various other projects I bet.

Well I’ve been out of work for ten years. No I’m just kidding. I’m doing fine. I’m going into my fifth year on the faculty at UCLA, which I’m very happy about. I enjoy my work there. And my band is doing just good. We play concerts. We don’t play all the time, but we play good concerts. We’ve just played The Playboy a few months ago, a couple of months ago, and last year this time Snooky and I were getting ready to go to Chicago to play the Chicago Jazz Festival together there with my band. And we made an album in between, right Snooky?
And so I’m really busy. I’m doing really good.
